item: prove the protoc-driven sample really links the repository's single taken-over redact runtime, by dependency closure rather than by scanning the main program
fix_retained: 1df0eb7 localized pkg/localdeps/go-wind-toolkit/protoc-gen-go-redact/redact/v1/redact.proto's go_package; the archive-identical protos under testdata/, examples/ and api/localdeps/redact were not touched and the original upstream archive is untouched

commands_actually_run_by_the_cases.binary_produced_by: go build -o protoc-gen-redact . inside the package, i.e. the taken-over plugin itself

mapping_check.M_flags_on_the_command_line: none. The cases pass no -M/--go_opt=M... mapping at all, so every generated import path comes from the go_package option of the proto files themselves. Nothing can quietly re-point an import back to upstream from the CLI, and equally nothing was fixed by adding one.
mapping_check.only_mapping_in_the_repository: api/buf.redact.gen.yaml managed override: file_option go_package path=redact/v1 value=go-wind-admin/pkg/localdeps/go-wind-toolkit/protoc-gen-go-redact/redact/v1;redact
mapping_check.grep_for_tx7do_in_generation_config: api/buf*.yaml and scripts/generate-redact.sh contain no tx7do mapping; the single hit is an explanatory comment in api/buf.yaml about the removed external buf.build/tx7do/pagination input
mapping_check.no_require_or_replace_or_download: go.mod and go.sum were not modified, no require line was restored, no replace was added and nothing was fetched from the upstream module to make these cases pass

generated_imports_recorded.compile: go build ./testdata/integration and go vet ./testdata/integration both exit 0 with the generated files present

dependency_closure.package_scanned: ./pkg/localdeps/go-wind-toolkit/protoc-gen-go-redact/testdata/integration (the actually generated sample package, not the server binary and not a build-tag view of it)
dependency_closure.redact_runtime_resolves_to: go-wind-admin/pkg/localdeps/go-wind-toolkit/protoc-gen-go-redact/redact/v1, i.e. the one runtime package in this repository, which is also the package the plugin binary and the server build link
dependency_closure.note: the sample directory is testdata, so go list ./pkg/... does not contain it at all (verified: 0 matches). That is why it is scanned explicitly here instead of inferred from the main program's closure.

honest_remainder.observed: test.pb.go carries one upstream string: the serialized descriptor embeds the go_package of the sample's own file, github.com/tx7do/go-wind-toolkit/protoc-gen-go-redact/testdata/integration;testdata
honest_remainder.why: testdata/integration/test.proto is deliberately still byte-identical to the locked archive, and protoc-gen-go bakes a file's own go_package into its descriptor
honest_remainder.why_it_is_not_a_dependency: it is a string inside the sample's self-description: not an import, not a module in the closure above, and the sample is not part of any build. The runtime package's own generated file redact/v1/redact.pb.go contains 0 occurrences of tx7do.
honest_remainder.decision: left as is rather than edited, because rewriting an archive-identical locked fixture to make a cosmetic string disappear is the wrong trade

buf_reentry_check.command: BUF=<pinned buf v1.60.0> bash scripts/generate-redact.sh in a clean worktree of c70c940
buf_reentry_check.tracked_file_changes: 0 (git status shows no modified tracked file; the only untracked entries were the evidence files this run wrote into that directory)
buf_reentry_check.meaning: regenerating through the normal Buf entry changes nothing beyond the already approved local go_package difference: extension field numbers, types and redaction rules are untouched, since the raw descriptor inside the generated file is byte-identical
buf_reentry_check.guard_also_satisfied: the script itself refuses buf other than 1.60.0 and fails if a duplicate redact output appears under api/gen/go/redact

case_results_reused.why_reuse_is_legitimate: the five cases, their inputs, the plugin sources, the proto fixtures and the toolchain digests are unchanged since 1df0eb7, so migration/patches/T15/T15-r3a-tools-integration.json stays the record of the 5-pass result
case_results_reused.what_was_re_run_here: make tools-integration (exit 0) in the worktree, plus the two generation subtests alone so the generated files could be inspected before their normal cleanup
case_results_reused.not_redone: T13's pristine-binary comparison and the rest of T13's tooling evidence

observation_not_act_on: scripts/generate-redact.sh line 8 sets GOFLAGS=-p=2, which replaces rather than appends to the caller's flags; the same clobbering was fixed in scripts/build-redact-plugin.sh under T13. It cannot rewrite go.mod here, because an explicitly set GOFLAGS suppresses the host go env value and the Go default is -mod=readonly, so the hazard that fix addressed is not live. It is recorded instead of changed, because touching a generation entry mid-round would invalidate the R4 evidence for no functional gain.
